name: Descend through the weather
summary: A full-bleed photograph of a peak above the cloud holds while the giant place name rises and goes soft over the cloud tops, then cloud climbs past its soft ghost and fills the screen with mist, and the frame clears from below onto a second, warmer aerial view of the place where a two-line statement lands. It is a first screen that arrives somewhere: a hotel, a valley, an outdoor school, a building in its landscape.
place: The first screen, as the hero, with the place's name as the h1 and the tagline as its sentence (the page's one action stays in the header bar); it hands over to a section that starts on the second photograph's dark ground. Once per page.
content: Two photographs of the place in the same light, both 2400px wide or more. Above the weather: a peak, ridge or headland over a cloud sea, with dark rock or a strong sky for the cloud to swallow (a picture that is already white reads as a fade to white) and a mid to dark lower third for the white name. Below it: an aerial or high view of the coast, valley, town or the property itself, its top quarter the palest part, its bottom third dark and calm, warmer than the first. The name: one word of 4-10 letters. A tagline of 8-14 words, a note of 3-7 words for the mist (a place and a height), a statement of two lines. The script grows its own cloud; a photograph of a cloud sea from above (tops) makes it real. Without two honest pictures of the place, from above and below, redraw.
options: hold 3 (2.4-4); phoneHold 2.2 (1.8-3); phone 'same' | 'rest'; scrub true with Lenis, else 0.8; tops none, the URL of a cloud-sea photograph keyed into the cloud (same origin or CORS, nothing but cloud in the crop); topsCrop [0,0,1,1]; wisps (defaults to tops), fog over darker ground for the near veil; wispsCrop [0,0,1,1]; art 'key' | 'alpha' (ready-made transparent cloud); seed 7, the grown cloud's shapes; fill 0.86 (0.6-0.94) share of the width the name fills; blur 14 (8-16) px on the lost copy of the name; feather 60 (40-80) svh of soft cloud edge; phoneFeather 40 (30-60); settle 1.2 (1.08-1.25) scale the second photograph settles from.
phone: The same descent with phone numbers: hold 2.2, a narrower far cloud with no sideways drift, the name fitted to the width, both photographs cropped to portrait (--above-pos, --below-pos).

name: Fly-through of photo cards
summary: The camera runs forward into one picture with a strong vanishing point (a jetty, a road, a long hall) while captioned photo cards grow out of the distance on alternating sides and pass the screen edges, one short statement changing at the top with each card. It turns five to twelve proof points, lines of a manifesto or views of a place into one journey through the subject's world.
place: In the middle of the page, after the hero: the intro, the work or the proof, where the visitor should feel the size of the subject's world. On the work it flies through the pieces themselves; before the work it holds three screens at most, so the work is not kept waiting. A quiet text section follows it.
content: One backdrop picture, landscape, 2400px wide or more, with a strong one-point perspective (a jetty, a road, a runway, a rail line, a long hall) whose lines meet on the vertical centre line, and a calm band above that point for the statement; or a 6-10 s muted forward move as a video encoded with a keyframe on every frame. Five to twelve card photographs (six hold three screens, and each more adds about 0.36), landscape 3:2 at 1200x800, at most two 4:5 portraits and never two in a row, all of the subject's world and all in one grade baked into the files; on the work, the cards are the work itself, each piece once. The cards stand apart from the backdrop: dim, soften or flatten the backdrop, or mat each card in the ground colour, so a card never melts into a busy picture of the same grade, and keep endScale near 4 so each card passes at more than half the screen's width. One statement per card, 4-7 words (about 34 characters); one caption per card, 1-4 words. Set --fly-vp, --fly-ground and --fly-focus-w to the backdrop's own lines. Without a picture whose lines meet at one point, or with photographs that cannot be made to look like one place, redraw.
options: inAir 3 (2-4) cards in the air at once; phoneInAir 2 (2-3); hold 0.36 a card slot, 3.3 for seven cards (1.5-6); sideX 0.32 (0.28-0.38) how far out the cards fly; endScale 4 (2.5-5): 4 a bold pass at the edge, 2.5 a calm drift; yaw 8 (0-10) degrees the cards turn inward, 0 flat; perspective 300 (240-600); title 1.3 (1-1.6) how much larger the first statement opens; dolly 1.8 for a still (1.6-2), 1.08 for a video (1-1.3); run 0.45 (0-0.7) how far the camera runs over the ground of a still, 0 for a backdrop with no ground; arrive true, a short settling beat at the end; haze 0 (0-0.3) fog left on the nearest card; count true, a plain "3 of 7" under the statement; phone 'same' | 'rest'; phoneMax 9 (3-12), more cards and the phone rests; phoneSideX 0.33 (0.1-0.45); phoneDy (0-40, measured when left out); phoneYaw 3 (0-10).
phone: The same fly-through with phone numbers: two cards in the air, each coming out at the foot of the focal object, growing to about 72% of the width and leaving through the bottom edge. More than nine cards and the phone gets the finished composition.

name: Powers-of-ten pull-back
summary: A full-bleed film or still shrinks until it is a screen on the wall of a real place, then the place shrinks until it is the picture in a framed print or a device resting on the page's ground: about an elevenfold pull-back in two reveals. Use it when the point is context: a reel shown in a room, a product in its setting, a thing at its true scale.
place: In the middle, on the section that shows the work or the product in use (the showcase, the work, the about). Its last frame is a section of its own, a headline, a sentence and a link beside the print, so it closes the argument it opens.
content: Three levels. The film: 16:9, 2560px wide, its subject in the centre third; a muted seamless loop of 8-20 s with a poster, a still, or a screen of the product. The place: a photograph seen straight on, 3:2 or 4:3, 3600px wide or more, with a calm wall for the screen (the scene draws its housing) or one rectangular opening (a window, a frame, a billboard) at 0.30-0.36 of its width and near its centre, and something around it that gives scale (a floor, a bench, a person); measure the opening into --wx --wy --ww --wh, and give a 4:5 crop for phones with its own -sm set. The object is built in CSS (a frame and mat, or a device bezel). Words, 60 at most: a title of 2-6 words and a sentence of 8-16 over the film, a wall label of 6-10 words, then a headline of 3-8 words, 18-32 words and a 2-3 word link. Without a place photograph whose opening can be measured, redraw.
options: jumps 2 (film, place, object) | 1 (film, place, ending full-bleed in the place); hold 3, 1.8 with one jump (1.5-4); holdPhone 2.6, 2.2 with one jump (1.6-3.2); depth 1.7 (1-2.2) the place's start scale, 1 a still wall, 2.2 strong parallax (needs a 4800px place); depthPhone 1.8; end 0.32 (0.24-0.44) the object's opening at the end, as a share of the width; endPhone 0.56 (0.4-0.7); side 'right' | 'left' where the object settles (for left also put class pb-side-left on the section); tilt 3 (0-6) degrees it turns as it settles; drop 0.02 (0-0.06); drift 0.08, 0 for a video (0-0.15), the slow zoom of a still; scrub 0.8, 0.4 with Lenis; phone 'same' | 'rest'.
phone: The same two reveals with a portrait print and the copy under it; hold 2.6.

name: Route journey
summary: A traveller (a top-down truck, a boat, a drone) stays parked on screen while a tilted map slides and turns under it along a route that draws itself, stopping at three to five stops where a board swings up and a gauge counts a real unit, until the camera cranes overhead and the destination, drawn as the subject itself, lights up from its centre out. Use it when the story really is a trip: a delivery, a tour, a supply chain, a process told as a road.
place: In the middle, on how it works or the about (the route a shipment, a walker or a season really takes), or as the contact when the way to the place is the story. The arrival line and its action close that part of the argument. Never for a plain list of steps, and only when the map can be drawn as the real place: a coast, a fjord or a mountain road is drawn as one, never as the demo's inland town.
content: One route as an SVG path in map pixels, 3000-4200 long, corners of 160px radius or more (300 at the stops), the first leg heading up the map; three to five stops (four by default), each with a 2-4 word title, a 25-40 word body and a gauge value in one real unit (km, days, metres, a year). A heading of 4-8 words, a lede of 30 words or fewer, an arrival line of 6-10 words and a 2-3 word action. Draw the map for this subject as the page's own .route-art, in the scene's classes so it takes the page's colours: the real route and what it really passes, with water, coast and relief where they really lie (traced from an open map of the place, in map px), and the destination drawn as the subject itself seen from above, as #route-dest (the house by the water, the shop front, the farm; never a grid of tiles), with the parts that light up on arrival classed .rd-lit. Without .route-art the scene rides a bare ground with only the road on it: honest but empty, a stand-in, never the place. The demo's town, lakes, fields and tile plot are placeholders, and a fjord or a coast shown as an inland town reads as the demo. The traveller is drawn in SVG; a cut-out of the real vehicle can replace it. Never invent a route for something that does not travel.
options: hold 1.6 + 0.8 a leg, 4.0 for four stops, at most 5 (1-6); phoneHold hold x 0.85; phone 'same' | 'rest'; scrub 0.6 (0-1), locked with Lenis; heading 'up' (the road ahead points up the screen) | 'north'; tilt 52 (0-62), 0 a flat map chase; phoneTilt 46; zoom 1.25 (1-1.5); phoneZoom 0.9; push 0.09 (0-0.12) push-in at each stop; phonePush 0.07; arrive 2.0 (1.3-2.4) zoom over the destination; phoneArrive 1.0; orbit 8 (0-12) degrees of swing at each stop; smooth 320 (160-400) map px of heading smoothing; plotGap 96 map px from the route's end to the centre of #route-dest; unit 'auto' or a step such as 0.5; perspective 1000 desktop, 900 compact, 760 phone (600-2400); bake true (the map is painted into bitmaps before the ride) | false.
phone: The same journey with phone numbers: tilt 46, zoom 0.9, the traveller centred, the intro across the top and the stops on a plate at the foot; hold 0.85 of the desktop's.

name: Warp jump
summary: Over a full-bleed field of radial streaks that speeds up and heats from ink into the accent with the scroll, a centred manifesto in capitals changes in timed beats, letters arriving out of the vanishing point and flying past the camera, until a disc of the accent opens at the centre and swallows the field into the next section. It is for one long statement on a technical, research or launch page, or (enter 'photo') the way from a photographic chapter into an abstract one.
place: In the middle, as the intro or the about: the page's principles in one ride. The section after it starts on the accent (any colour with exit 'release'). Once per page. Three beats (the anchor with one ending, up to four principles, the final line) hold three screens, since the hold is one screen a beat; more beats only on a page with no other long scene.
content: No pictures. Words written fresh for the subject, 35-60 in all: an anchor of 1-2 words (10 letters or fewer); two or three endings of 2-4 words (16 letters or fewer, 12 on a phone); three to twelve principles of two short sentences each (4-8 words, 40 letters or fewer); a final line of 3-6 words on two lines. One accent of any hue but violet, indigo or purple, light enough to read as a 1px line on black. enter 'photo' adds one photograph 1600px wide or more (an aerial view, terrain, a machine, a city at night) and a lead sentence of 8-16 words.
options: exit 'disc' (an accent disc swallows the field) | 'flood' (the streaks become a tunnel of accent that closes like an iris) | 'release' (no exit; the field holds and the page scrolls on); enter 'field' | 'photo' (opens on a photograph and zooms through it, one more screen); speed 1 (0.5-1.4) and accentMax 0.5 (0.2-0.7), the restraint dials: 0.5 and 0.25 calm, 1.4 and 0.7 a loud launch; rays 1100 (600-1600); hold beats (3-8), one screen a beat; phoneHold beats (3-7); phone 'same' | 'rest'; scrub 0.5; count true, a plain "2 of 4" while the beats run; progressVar false.
phone: The same ride with fewer rays and the principles in a centred column, four at most a beat, standing in a dark mouth of the column's shape (a tablet held upright too); hold one screen a beat.

name: Light flood
summary: One sentence on a held stage plays out a day: a soft dome of colour rises behind it like a sun, swells until the whole screen is lit, then night falls from the top and the last light sinks and goes out on the next section's dark ground, while the setup words go out of focus and the key phrase, lit by the dome, stays sharp. It gives one statement three screens of weight: a brand chapter, a turn from day to night for a hotel or a spa, a promise on a finance page.
place: In the middle, between the hero and the detail, as the intro or the about; or as the last word before the booking or the action. The section after it starts on the night colour. Once per page.
content: No pictures. One sentence in two lines of 18 characters or fewer each, spaces and punctuation counted: a lead of 2-4 setup words, which must read alone as the title for the first quarter, and a key phrase of 2-3 words. Nothing else on the stage: no body copy, buttons, labels or logos. Six colours (day, halo, core, night, ink, key) or a checked preset; the core needs a relative luminance of 0.15-0.25.
options: palette '' | 'dusk' | 'sky' | 'sage' (sets all six colours); direction 'dusk' (day, light, night) | 'dawn' (night, light, day; add class lf--dawn); ending 'night' | 'flood' (holds on the full flood; add class lf--flood); focus 'rack' (the lead goes soft, the key comes sharp) | 'flat' (opacity only); hold 3 (2-4); phoneHold 2.5 (2-4); flood 3 (2.4-3.6) end scale of the dome; phoneFlood 3.6 (2.4-4.2); scrub 0.6; header '', the selector of a fixed header, and headerClass 'is-dark', the class it gets while the night is under it; phone 'same' | 'rest'.
phone: The same day with phone numbers: a broad, low dome, smaller blur steps; hold 2.5.

name: Shaped edge carries the new ground
summary: A photograph with a wide, even sky zooms slowly while a field painted exactly in the sky's colour rises over it as a full-width arch, a short heading spreading word by word along its curve, until the arch has passed the top and the field is the flat ground of the next chapter, whose title turns in letter by letter over a small picture. It is a chapter divider for places, buildings, travel and property: the sky seems to come loose and become the page.
place: Between two sections: it ends one chapter on its photograph and opens the next (the intro, the rooms, the gallery, the contact) on the sky's colour, which the next section keeps. Two or three a page at most, each on a different photograph and ground.
content: One photograph, 3:2 or 16:10, 3000px wide or more, with open, even sky in the top third and a subject that runs edge to edge across the lower half (a range, a skyline, terraces, a shore; a single tower on a big sky hides the move), plus a 2:3 crop for phones. One small inset picture, 2:1, 1200x600 or more, from the next chapter. --ground sampled from the photograph's sky (the median of a 5% patch in the top third), never chosen by eye, and --ink at 7:1 on it. Words: a headline of 3-6 words and a lede of 14 or fewer; an arc heading of 4 words (6 at most on desktop, 34 characters); a statement of 6-10 words; a chapter title of 1-3 words (16 characters). Without a photograph with that sky, redraw.
options: hero 'sky' (the headline in --ink straight on the sky) | 'band' (a flat translucent fill behind it and white type, for a busy top left); zoom 1.5 (1.2-1.8) end scale of the photograph; phoneZoom 1.3 (1.1-1.5); fade false (true also fades the photograph as it zooms, for dusk or interiors); arc 'spread' | 'static'; spread 0.10 (0.04-0.12) the widest word gap; phoneSpread 0.08 (0.04-0.10); chrome '', the selector of a fixed header, with chromeLight '#fff' its ink over the photograph and chromeX (0-100) for a centred logo; scrub 0.6; phone 'same' | 'rest'. The hold is not an option: the CSS sets it from the arch's height (2.25 screens by default).
phone: The same scene with a tall arch that reads as a doorway and an arc heading of four words at most. Under 600px tall, or with a longer heading, the phone gets the finished composition.

name: Stepped columns raise a stage
summary: A row of three to five columns of short copy on one flat page colour fills with solid ink from the foot, each column at its own pace, so the row reads first as a falling bar chart and then levels into one block, the copy turning from ink on the page to page on the ink; where ink has arrived a square wheel rolls over a road of arches, gaining a side at every arch until it rests as a circle. It is for a process or a set of tiers that really runs from rough to smooth, on a page that can commit to one bold colour.
place: In the middle, on how it works, the steps or the tiers of the pricing. Keep the wheel only when the steps' own words go from rough to smooth (a board planed true, a road resurfaced); a timeline, a pre-order or price tiers take {"wheel":"none"} for a plain stepped chart. Keep the default {"ghost":false}: each column opens as an ink stub that already holds its copy, so no ink edge crosses words being read.
content: No pictures, no footage, no icons. A heading of 8 words or fewer on two lines at most; an optional rail with two one-word ends (Rough, Smooth); per step an optional note in plain words (never an index number), a title of two short lines (18 characters a line) and 16-28 words, whose optional .sr-more part the phone drops (keep the rest to 70 characters). Three to five steps is the design; up to twelve run as rows. Exactly two colours: one flat page colour and one ink at 4.5:1 or more.
options: hold 0.6 a step, 1.8-3 (2.4 for four; 1.8 with wheel 'none'); phoneHold 0.5 a step, 1.8-2.6; scrub 0.5, 0.3 with Lenis (0.2-0.8); order 'descending' (the first column fills first) | 'ascending' (a rising chart, for tiers) | 'centre' (odd counts); ends [0.30, 0.86], when the first and the last column are full (first 0.20-0.40, last 0.75-0.88); wheel 'road' | 'none'; ghost false (each column opens as an ink stub that already holds its copy) | true (the copy waits in ink on the page and the rising edge jumps past it).
phone: The scene turns 90 degrees: stacked rows turn to ink one after another, each in one short fade (a sideways wipe would cut its words), and the wheel rolls along the header's rail in ink on the page colour; hold about 2 for four steps.

name: Orbit to formation
summary: One set of square photographs rides a single invisible wheel that changes shape as the page scrolls: a huge arch turning over the opening statement, then a ring closing round one big figure, then a half-wheel at the edge of the screen beside a column of figures that light one by one. It is one continuous set piece for a team, a culture, a gallery or an archive, in place of three separate galleries.
place: In the middle, on the about, the gallery or the figures: the stretch that says who the people are or how long the place has been there. Set {"hold":4} (the file's own default of 5 is for a page with no other scene); it is still the page's one long scene. Not on the work: its cards are small, so the work is shown at size elsewhere.
content: Twelve to sixteen distinct square photographs (14 by default; phones use the first ten), 560px or more, in one grade, the subject inside the central 60% so a tilted or upside-down card still reads. Never the same picture twice, at most two from one source (one film, one shoot, one building) and never side by side; with fewer than twelve distinct pictures, redraw rather than repeat them (the script repeats a short set whole, which reads as padding). People, hands and studio moments only when they are the client's own; otherwise real pictures of its world (archive photographs, the place, its materials), never stand-ins for its team. A statement of 6-10 words that holds two lines (about 45 characters keeps the full size). One figure of 4 glyphs or fewer (a year, a count) with an optional second line of 3 words or fewer, and a caption of 12 words or fewer. Four rows of figures (2-6 work), each of 4 glyphs or fewer with a label of 4 words or fewer: real facts about the subject from the brief (a year, a height, a number of rooms or days), never invented business numbers, never a constant of the medium (25 frames a second) or a figure worked out from another on the list; count true only with such real figures.
options: hold 5 (4-7); phoneHold 4 (3-6); scrub 0.6, locked with Lenis; radius 1 (0.7-1.6) the arch's radius as a share of the width, 0.7 steep, 1.6 flat; crest 0.24 (0.18-0.30) height of the arch's top card; phoneCrest 'auto' or 0.14-0.44; ring 0.46 (0.36-0.48) the ring's width, spilling past the frame from 0.44; stagger 0.2 (0-0.5) how far the cards peel off one after another; wind 'close' | 'spring'; tilt 1 (the faces follow the wheel) or 0.2-0.9 (the faces stay near upright); dim 0.4 (0.4-0.8) opacity of a figure row off the reading line; count false (true counts each figure up as it lights); phone 'same' | 'rest'; phoneCards 10 (6-14).
phone: The same wheel with phone numbers: a tall ten-card ring, then the wheel sinks to the bottom edge instead of rolling aside and the figures rise out from behind it; hold 4.

name: Scatter and lock
summary: One photograph is cut into a grid of live cells scattered as twisted, depth-blurred shards through real 3D space; the scroll flies them home from the centre out into a gapped contact sheet, snaps them shut with a short flash and grows the finished picture to full bleed. It opens a showreel, a body of work, a brand mark or a chapter on how a thing is made, from one strong picture.
place: In the middle, as the door to the work or the showcase. Its last frame is the picture at full bleed, so the next section can carry on from it: a reel that opens on the same frame, or the picture held while the next section rises over it. Once per page.
content: One landscape photograph, 16:9 at 1920 and 3200px (it ends at about 1.55x), with one strong subject near the centre, texture in every part of the frame (moss, water, rock, foliage: every shard must read as a piece of a photograph, not a grey square), mid to light in tone; plus a 4:5 crop at 1000 and 1600px for phones. Served with CORS and never lazy-loaded. A headline of two lines; an optional caption of up to 24 words; an optional poster word of 12 characters or fewer and a short corner note on the poster. Without one picture strong enough to be the whole screen, redraw.
options: mode 'assemble' | 'explode' (the poster shatters at the end; never as the first section); hold 2.5 (1.5-4); phoneHold 2 (1.5-3); scrub 0.6 (0-0.8); cols 7 and rows 4, at most 40 cells (5x3 calm, 8x5 a swarm); phoneCols 4 and phoneRows 5, at most 20; heroes 'auto' (the most detailed cells in front) | 'fixed' | a list of [col, row] nearest first; phoneHeroes 'auto'; perspective 1200 (700-2000), phonePerspective 900; depth 2000 (600-3000), phoneDepth 1200; near 280 (0-300), phoneNear 160; twist 40 (0-45), 0 a flat glide like dealt cards; drift 0.06 (0-0.15); order 'centre' | 'sweep' | 'random'; blur true; flash 0.16 (0-0.3); handoff true (the poster grows to full bleed) | false (it rests framed); wordFit true; seed 11; phone 'same' | 'rest'.
phone: The same assembly on a 4x5 grid over the 4:5 crop, the headline at the top; hold 2.

name: Arrive and settle on a sideways track
summary: A held row slides sideways with the scroll and each item's height and tilt come from where it is on screen, so the letters of one giant closing line enter scattered at the right edge, swoop through their line and settle by the middle; then the camera pulls back until the whole line fits, ending on a calm frame with the line whole and a button. Its default is the page's last word and its action; the stair preset makes it a staircase of testimonials and the rise preset a short track of projects.
place: At the end of the page, as the call to action before the footer. With a preset it can carry the testimonials (stair, real quotes only) or the work (rise) instead. A quiet section comes before it.
content: Type preset: one line of 3-5 words, 14-28 characters, a question or an invitation, its first word of four letters or more and no word over 16 characters; a support line of 6-12 words and a button of 2-3 words. No pictures: the type is the picture, on one flat ground. The end frame shows the whole line, verb included: read the 100% frame at 1440, 768 and 390, and if it rests on the last words alone, shorten the line or set it smaller. The line is set at --display-weight (600 when the page sets none): set that token to a weight the page loads, or load 600 of the display face. Stair preset: a heading of six words or fewer and 5-7 real quotes of 25-45 words, each with name, role and a square portrait. Rise preset: a heading of up to five words and one sentence, 3-5 projects each with a 1.46:1 picture, a 1-3 word title, 12-20 words and a link, and one closing sentence with an action.
options: preset 'type' | 'stair' | 'rise' (the data-settle attribute); speed 0.7-1.3, px of sideways travel per px of scroll (1 type, 1 stair, 1.2 rise; the hold is measured from it, 1-4 screens); rest 0.2-0.6 screens of still end frame (0.3); amp 0.6-1.5 letter offset in letter heights (1.5); tilt 0-20 degrees (18; cards 0); lift 20-60 vh card offset (36 stair, 60 rise); curve 'swoop' | 'calm' | 'linear' (swoop type, linear stair, calm rise); settle 0.30-0.60 share of the width by which an item has settled (0.45, 0.30, 0.50); enter 1.00-1.25 where the move begins (1.04, 1.20, 1.20); inset px of a fixed header to keep the letters clear of (0); scrub true with Lenis, else 0.5.
phone: No pin and no sideways travel: the line stands stacked as in the finished composition, its letters swooping onto their lines as each line rises up the screen, and the support line and button rise in after them; cards rise 16vh each.

name: Sideways walk through rooms
summary: A full-height row of flat-coloured rooms is walked sideways at one screen of width per screen of scroll, each room with its own moment (a photograph that swaps in a frame, portraits that open while a statement brightens, a word that climbs, three value words that shear apart, project strips that open one after another), until a last room slides over a held column and the whole row pulls away to uncover the closing headline. It is a guided tour of a studio, a building or a body of work that ends on the contact.
place: From the middle to the end of the page: the work, the projects or the tour of the building, handing over to the contact, whose ground it ends on. About ten screens: it is a whole page on its own (the work, the about and the contact in one), over the six screens the draw gives all of a page's scenes, so it is never dealt beside another scene. Build it only when the client's own photographs carry the whole page, with the hero and at most one short section around it, and nothing loud after it.
content: Fourteen photographs of the client's own work or building, from one shoot or in one grade: a wide interior (2200px or more) and two views of one room, close and wide, for the photo room; two 3:4 portraits; five landscape project pictures with the subject centred; two more for the held column; two at 16:9 for the last room. Words, about 280: a threshold headline of two lines and a lede of 25-35 words; a two-line heading and about 30 words for the photo room; a statement of 35-45 words in five lines; one chapter word; three value words of 13 characters or fewer with a note; five projects (a name of 14 characters or fewer, a year, a place, a link); a question of two lines with 40-60 words; two captions; a closing headline of 2-4 words. Rooms can be left out; the photographs cannot: without the client's own pictures, redraw.
options: rate 0.8-1.25 screen widths walked per screen of scroll (1); ramp 0.15-0.35 screens the walk takes to start and stop (0.25); open 50-66 vw, an open project card (60); closed 12-18 vw, a waiting strip (15); stack 0.5-1.2 screens held on the column while its photos stack (0.7); swap 0.5-1 screens held on the last room's photo swap (0.5); rest 0.2-0.6 screens of still closing headline (0.3); scrub 0.3 with Lenis, else 0.6 (0.1-1.5); intro true, the threshold title rises once when the walk is on screen at load. The hold is measured from the rooms: 10.5 screens for the full set with five cards, 0.6 more a card.
phone: Below 900px wide or on a portrait screen: no pin and no sideways travel; the rooms stand as a vertical column in the same colour order, each with its own small scrubbed move.

name: Hinged sheets
summary: Two to four tickets rise together from a face-down deck below the fold, each peeling off, turning from its ink-coloured back to its paper front on a shared vanishing point and landing in its slot one by one, after the headline has stepped back to the top of the stage, where it stays, sharp, as the heading over the row. It is for prices, passes, letters or figures on a page with a real paper, ticket or print idea; without that idea the turn is a trick.
place: In the middle, on the pricing, the tickets or the figures. The section's heading stays readable throughout: the headline rises and shrinks to the top of the stage before the deck reaches it and stays there as the heading over the finished row, never a blurred ghost behind the landed tickets.
content: Two to four tickets (three reads best; five or more run as the flow version), every front with the same amount of copy: a name of 1-2 words, a pitch of up to 26 words (10-16 with a photograph), 2-3 points of 2-5 words, a price with what it buys, an optional action; every back one or two short words set very large, the brand and a small line. A headline of 4-7 words on two lines, an optional sentence under it, a line over the row of 3-8 words, and fine print of 15-25 words. At rest the row reads as printed tickets, not pricing cards: type set to the edges of the stub, the copy filling the sheet, the page's own corners (square when its buttons are). A photograph on the top 29% of a ticket only when it is the ticket's own picture (a show's poster), never one already used on the page. One ink (--accent) for the backs and every word, a paper colour, and two tints of a ground.
options: hold 1.2-4 (0.6 + 0.5 a ticket: 2.1 for three); scrub true with Lenis, else 0.5 (0.2-0.6); deck 0-1 (1) how far the tickets start towards one centre deck, 0 rises each from its own slot; stagger 0.08-0.18 (0.14; 0.12 with four); wobble 0-8 degrees (7); lean 0-18 degrees (16); lift 0-120 px towards the viewer at mid-turn (120); phone 'flip' | 'rest'.
phone: No held stage: the tickets stand in a column, and each rises, turns and lands on its own as it scrolls in, face-up and still before it is read. Tablets, short windows and more than four tickets get the same.

name: Fly into the shape
summary: The brand's own solid mark rises with the content to the centre of the screen with the title set in light type on its face, turns to face the visitor, and then the camera flies at it, so the next chapter's picture shows through its face and rushes past every edge of the screen while the title grows with it to full size, never crossed by an edge. It is the doorway into a dark or immersive chapter, and with data-dir "out" the way back out at its end.
place: Between two sections: the end of a light part of the page and the door into a dark one (the work, the showcase, the about), whose ground is exactly the world's night colour. At most twice a page, in and out.
content: One closed SVG path of the brand's own mark (a monogram, an emblem, a building's silhouette, a keyhole) with a solid core: an inscribed circle of at least 15% of its box. A thin-stroked logo or a plain circle does not work. One landscape photograph of the chapter's world, 16:10 or 16:9, 2000px or more, dark (mean luminance about 20% or less) with a calm centre and a dark bottom edge, and a 9:16 crop for phones; or a 6-10 s muted loop of 4MB or less. A title of 2-6 words on two lines (12 characters a line at most), a sub-line of 10-18 words, an optional aside of 3-6 words. Without an ownable mark, redraw.
options: dir 'in' | 'out' (prefer the data-dir attribute); hold 2 (1.4-2.6); phoneHold 1.6 (1.2-2.4); size 0.4 (0.2-0.6) the mark's box as a share of the height, px above 1, or 'fit' (the title is set on its face, smaller when the mark cannot hold it at full size, and the mark at rest stays 16px inside the stage); phoneSize 'fit' | 0.3-0.75 | px 64-420; turn 45 (0-180) degrees; phoneTurn 12; depth 0.06 (0-0.15) thickness of the extruded side; phoneDepth 0.05; ease 'fly' (a steady camera) | 'sine.inOut' | 'none'; zoom 1.4 (1-1.8) how far the world's picture grows over the hold; blur 0 (0-6) px on the world through the fastest part, desktop only; scrub 0.8, true with Lenis; phone 'same' | 'rest'.
phone: The same dive with the mark sized to hold the whole title on its face (16px inside the screen; the title set smaller when the screen is too narrow for both), a smaller turn and a shorter hold (1.6).

name: Shape-shifting window over a fixed world
summary: One full-bleed photograph of a place stays still behind a shutter in the page's ground colour with two offset tall windows cut in it; the scroll slides the windows level (up to the title above the low one and down to the caption under the high one, never across a word), closes the bar between them, then scales the shutter past the screen edges so the visitor pushes through into the place while one chapter word rises in. It lets one strong, wide picture of a building, a room or a landscape carry the opening title and the name of the first chapter.
place: The first screen, as the hero (the page's one action stays in the header bar), opening onto the first chapter, which is the place itself. The page's ground is one flat colour that the shutter matches exactly.
content: One landscape photograph of the place, 3:2 or 16:10, about 3600px wide, with a diagonal of interest from lower left to upper right (each window frames something at the start), a calm top third for the word and nothing important on the vertical centre line; a 9:16 crop for phones; or a muted 8-12 s loop with little motion and the still as its poster. Two optional props for the bottom corners (foliage, a lamp, a chair), as cut-outs or keyed from a photograph of something dark against a bright sky. A title of 4-7 words on two lines (about 25 characters), a caption of 10-18 words (wide screens only, and left out where it does not fit under the windows, so repeat its key fact in the lede), one chapter word of 6-12 letters, and a lede of 18-32 words with a 2-3 word link.
options: hold 2.4 (1.8-3); phoneHold 2.0 (1.6-2.6); stagger 0.16 (0.08-0.165) how far each window starts off the shared band, 0.08 a calm diptych; phoneStagger 0.08 (0.05-0.12); bar 'auto' or 8-24 px of ground between the windows; high 'right' | 'left', the window that starts high; overscan 1.08 (1.04-1.15); phoneOverscan 1.16 (1.04-1.2); worldScale 0.8 (0.75-1) the world's start scale; wordTop 80 px (phoneWordTop 72); wordWidth 0.92 (0.6-0.96; phoneWordWidth 0.86); parallax 0.2 (0-0.3); scrub 0.6, true with Lenis; phone 'same' | 'rest'.
phone: The same push with two slim windows across 85% of the width, the title full width above them, no caption and the word fitted to 86% of the width; hold 2. Portrait tablets get the same.

name: Twin-image scanner
summary: Two registered pictures of one subject are stacked, its surface (a photograph on the light ground) and its structure (a line drawing on the dark ground), and a scan line rising with the scroll rewrites everything it passes, headline included, from the first into the second, then names the parts it found. It is the look under the hood: a machine, a product, a building, a before and after.
place: In the middle, on the features or how it works: the moment the page shows what is inside. The section after it starts on the dark ground.
content: Two pictures of the same thing on the same 4:5 canvas, 1600x2000 or more, registered pixel for pixel: a cut-out photograph or render of the client's own product, machine or building, and a line drawing of the same framing (two passes from one 3D camera, or traced over the photograph at 1:1; dashed lines for the hidden parts, the accent only on the core). With only a photograph shot on white, data-trace="lines" draws the structure from its edges, which shows nothing hidden. A headline of 4-8 words on two lines, two tags of 1-2 words naming the two materials, 1-12 callouts of 3 words or fewer naming real parts (three read best, one marked is-focus), an outro of 18-30 words and a 2-3 word action. Without the subject's own photograph or render, redraw.
options: hold 2.5 (1.5-3); phoneHold 2 (1.5-3); park 92 (80-96) where the line waits at the start, % of the stage from the top; phonePark 88; focus null (the is-focus callout's dot) or 30-70, the centre of the slow band; band 16 (12-24) its height; slow 0.56 (0.4-1) speed inside the band; scale 1.12 (1-1.16) the subject's start scale, phoneScale 1.08; wake 5 (0-10) the accent band under the line; detail 1 (0.6-1.6) trace sensitivity; scrub 0.6, true with Lenis; debug true, to check the registration. Framing on the section: --ts-zoom (1-2.4), --ts-fx, --ts-fy, --ts-phone-zoom, --ts-edge.
phone: The same scan in one column, the words above and the subject below, the outro taking the headline's place at the end; hold 2. Under 360px wide or 640px tall, the finished composition.

name: Instrument dial stage
summary: A stage drawn like an instrument reads off three to six items one at a time: a wide dial arc lights tick by tick to each item's own number, a bezel clicks round to it, the item's name stands huge on the horizon and its picture rises to stand under the name on a ground that surges up and settles. It gives a few products, materials, places or stages, each with one number, an engineered reveal.
place: In the middle, on the features, the range, the figures, a few projects with one number each, or the stages of a climb or a process.
content: Three to six items (up to twelve work; the hold grows), each with a name of one word, 8 letters or fewer (it becomes the huge word); one 4:5 picture, 840x1050 or more, all from the same angle and in the same light (photographs of the products when the items are products; otherwise real pictures of each item's world, as the demo's four heights of one climb); a line of a few words; one value with its unit (9 characters or fewer) and a caption of 4 words or fewer. Each picture shows its own item, and its caption names only what the picture shows. Optional data-at (the reading on the dial) and data-tone (the item's ground); give range and data-at when the items are readings on one scale, so the dial reads as an instrument. A heading of 6-10 words on two lines. Not for long copy or items with more than one number.
options: hold 0.85 an item + 0.6, at most 7 (the phone holds 0.9 of it); scrub 0.8 or true; grow 0.28 (0.18-0.40) start scale of the first name; ticks about one every 12px of arc (16-200); range [low, high] of the scale; turn 1.2 (0-3) degrees each picture rolls; tilt true, the pictures lean toward a fine pointer; field true (each item's own ground below the horizon) | false; wash true (the incoming ground washes over the name before it settles); snap false; phone 'same' | 'rest'.
phone: The same dial with phone numbers: the ring fitted under the heading, the list of items hidden, the value full width at the foot; hold 0.9 of the desktop's.

name: Lens over a thumbnail stream
summary: A held strip of greyscale thumbnails grouped by project slides left under a playhead line, and every picture near the line swells, takes its colour and heaps into a collage of its project before sinking back, while a masthead caption relays letter by letter to name the project under the line. It turns a whole archive or portfolio into one scrubbable index with the detail view built in.
place: In the middle, on the work, the archive or the catalogue, where a grid of project cards would otherwise go.
content: Five or six projects of five to ten pictures each, 25-60 in all (five hold about three screens: set {"hold":3}, since the file's own clamp starts at four; each project more adds about 0.6): one landscape key picture a project (about 960px wide) and the rest in mixed orientations (480-640px on the long side), each with its real width and height, never cropped. They are the client's own: its work, its collection, its products. Per project a name of 1-2 words, a year, a category of 2-3 words and a link; a section title of 2-3 words and a line with the range of years. With fewer than five projects, use a plain index instead.
options: hold clamp(0.62 a project, 4, 7.5) (2-10); phoneHold clamp(0.55 a project, 3.5, 6.5) (2-10); phone 'same' (a fixed lens in the centre) | 'rest' (the contact sheet); sweep 0.5 (0-0.6) share of the width the line travels, 0 a fixed lens; bloom 9 (4-10) the key picture's height in bloom units; phoneBloom 9 (4-10); reach 0.36 (0.15-0.8; phone 0.7) the lens radius; gate 0.35 (0.15-1): 0.15 one collage at a time, 1 two always mix; push 0.35 (-0.55 dense to 0.35 roomy; phone -0.55); dwell 0.7 (0-0.9) how much the strip slows at each project; seed 0, reshuffles the collages; scrub 0.6, locked with Lenis.
phone: The same index with a fixed lens in the centre and the strip doing the travel, six pictures a project; hold about 4.4 for eight projects.

name: Pinned chapter switcher
summary: One held full-bleed stage plays three to six picture chapters, the scroll driving a hard-edged wipe between each pair (from the right, out of the corner, then rising from the bottom), with the title and text swapping at the half-and-half frame and a progress bar for each chapter filling as it goes. It is for feature chapters, before and after, the parts of a day or the variants of a product, where every chapter has its own picture and its own words.
place: In the middle, on the features, the work, the stages of a day or the variants: wherever the page has three to six parallel things to say.
content: Three to six chapters (four by default), each with one full-bleed picture, shot or chosen as one series: the same horizon height, the same subject in different states or in different light, a hard change of colour between neighbours, the subject above the horizon or in the right two thirds and calm ground low on the left for the words. Give each a square main crop, a 3:5 crop for upright tablets and a 2:5 crop for phones, and its data-horizon. Per chapter a tab name of 14 characters or fewer, a title of 2-5 words and a body of 25-40 words (30 or fewer for phones); a section heading of 2-5 words. Muted loops can replace the pictures. Not for a run of similar photographs.
options: wipes 'mixed' (right, corner, rise) | one wipe name for every chapter ('right' makes a before-and-after stepper) | a list such as 'right,drop,corner' | 'pair' (two framed pictures a chapter on the ground, the words beside them); length 1 (0.8-1.4) screens a chapter; wipe 0.5 (0.35-0.7) share of a chapter spent wiping; horizon auto (0.2-0.8); shade 0.25 (0-0.6); push 1 (0-1.5); index 'tabs' | 'bars' | 'none'; counter true, a rolling "2 of 4"; preroll true; scrub 0.6 (0.4 on a phone), true with Lenis; maxHold 6 (3-8); phone 'same' | 'rest'; phoneLength 0.85; phoneWipe 0.55; phoneMax 6. Per chapter: data-wipe, data-horizon, data-horizon-at, --plate-bg, --scrim (0.45), --obj-pos, --obj-pos-phone.
phone: The same wipes with phone numbers (0.85 screen a chapter) on the 2:5 crops. More than six chapters, or a screen under 560px tall, gets the finished composition.

name: Fixed hero object
summary: One product stays on its own layer and turns with the scroll while the page's chapter panels rise beneath it one screen at a time: from the centre of the hero it flies to a lane beside a heading, crosses to the other side beside a spec sheet as a dark ground rises under it, then docks small and centred above a gauge and its numbers. It is for the launch of one piece of hardware (a camera, a watch, a drone, a bottle) that has a turntable render.
place: The first screen and the two sections after it (the hero, a feature and the specifications, with the figures and the action in the dock) as one held stretch of about five and a half screens, which replaces those sections; each chapter more adds 1.75 screens, so a third is only for a page with no other scene. The page's one action stays in the header bar until the dock. Once per page.
content: A turntable image sequence of the product: 36-120 frames (72 at 1280x960 for desktop, 36 at 960x720 for phones), transparent WebP or AVIF, rendered round a vertical axis from 10-15 degrees above, frame 0 the three-quarter beauty pose, no floor shadow, the widest pose 86-90% of the frame. A hero title of two lines and a caption of 24 words or fewer. One to four chapters, each with a heading of two lines (each line in a .fho-line), a paragraph or a spec sheet of 3-12 rows, and data-frame naming the pose its copy talks about; an optional dock with a gauge (--fho-v), one to four readouts that count up, and an action. Without a turntable render, redraw: a still alone does not turn.
options: frames, the URL pattern of the sequence ({000} zero-padded, {i} plain; without it the still stands in, unturned); count 72 (36-120); phoneFrames and phoneCount (phones, upright tablets, touch screens); wideFrames and wideCount (an optional 2000x1500 set for wide 2x screens); turns auto (1-3); hold auto, 1.75 a panel (7 for four); phoneHold auto, 1.5 a panel; hero 1.2 (0.9-1.3) scale of the opening pose; park 1.6 (1.15-1.9) largest scale in the right lane; left 1.15 (0.9-1.3); bleed 8 (0-14) vw past the right edge; dock 0.62 (0.5-0.7); bank 7 (0-10) degrees into each flight; sweep 12 (0-16) degrees of rock in the left lane; counter true, a small "2 of 4"; intro true; scrub 0.8, true with Lenis; phone 'same' | 'rest'. Per chapter: data-frame, data-lane 'left' | 'right'.
phone: The vertical route: no sideways flights; the object rises from the centre into the room above the copy, which sits at the foot of the screen, and docks above the gauge; the 36-frame set; hold 1.5 a panel.

name: Scrubbed transformation sequence
summary: One object goes through one change of state as the page scrolls (raw to finished, closed to open, lifted and handed over), played as a frame sequence on a canvas while the ground opens from the page colour to the after colour, the thing it came from slides away, the thing it ends on rises under it and callouts land on the finished object. Use it only when there are 80-250 rendered or filmed frames, with alpha, of the object changing.
place: In the middle, on the showcase or how it is made, or as the page's finale before the action: the before statement opens it and the after line with one action closes it.
content: A frame sequence of the object changing, about 120 frames (80-250), square with alpha, from a locked-off camera, the object filling most of the frame with its foot in the same place at the end: desktop frames about twice the box's size (1600px), a phone set of every second frame (about 1000px). Optional cut-outs of the before context (what it came from) and the receiver (the plinth, shelf or pad it ends on), rendered by the same cameras. A before statement of 5-7 words (36 characters at most) as the headline, up to six callouts of 2-6 words placed on the last frame's silhouette (three is right), an after line of 3-6 words and a 2-3 word action. Never fake it by turning one still: without the footage, redraw.
options: frames, the desktop URL pattern (#### is the zero-padded index; required, else the finished composition); count 120 (2-400; 80-250 for a good scrub); phoneFrames and phoneCount (60 with its own pattern); hold 4 (3-5); phoneHold 3 (2-4); scrub 0.6, 0.3 with Stage.smooth(); split 0.85 (0.5-0.95) share of the frames played evenly; ground 'iris' | 'none' (keeps the page colour); irisAt [0.5, 0.54] where the disc grows from; push 1.25 (1-1.4) how far the camera starts pushed in; firstBox [0.17, 0.3, 0.83, 0.81] the object's outline in the first frame; centre true, the object glides to the centre while the title is away (laptop).
phone: The same fractions on the phone frame set, the object centred and wider than the screen, the after line in a top slot and the callouts as a stack of up to four rows under it; hold 3. Data-saving visitors get the finished composition and download no frames.

name: Picture develops from marks
summary: A near full-width pen drawing is laid down by the scroll, heaviest strokes first, then the hatching, then the faint construction lines, each stroke growing along its length with a wet tip in the accent that dries to ink, while the camera pulls back from a close-up of its densest part to the whole sheet. It is for a subject that owns drawn material (sketches, plans, maps, engravings) and a story about process; for a photograph, mode 'darkroom' develops the print, shadows first.
place: In the middle, on how it works, the about or the work, where the drawing being made is the argument. Once per page.
content: One drawing, landscape 2:1 to 2.4:1, dark ink on white or on transparency (SVG best, PNG, JPEG only at q85 or better), 8-24% of its area inked, with three visible tiers (heavy outlines, mid hatching, faint construction lines) drawn with a heavy, loose pen: 5px or more for the heavy tier at display size, since hairlines break into dust. The client's own sketches or plans, an old map or an engraving from the open collections, or a drawing made in code from the subject itself; served same-origin or with CORS. An optional portrait crop (0.8-0.95:1) for phones. A title of 3-7 words on two lines, a note of 25-40 words, and a caption of 2-8 words naming the subject and the medium. For a photograph, mode 'darkroom'.
options: mode 'ink' | 'darkroom'; hold 2 (1.6-3.5); phoneHold 1.5 (1.2-2.6); phone 'same' | 'rest'; sweep 'radial' | 'tl-down' | 'down' | 'up' | 'right' | 'left'; focus, the origin of a radial sweep as 'x% y%' (default zoomFocus); inkWeight 0.40 (0.25-0.60), higher is stricter darkest-first; sweepWeight 0.36 (0.20-0.60); coarse 0.14 (0-0.20); fine 0 (0-0.06; darkroom 0.12); edge 'accent' | 'off'; band 0.10 (0.04-0.16) width of the wet edge; strength 0.9 (0.5-1); start 0.16 (0.06-0.24) share already drawn at the start; phoneStart 0.24; scale 1.6 (1-1.8) the opening close-up, 1 turns the camera off; zoomFocus '44% 46%', put it on the densest part of the drawing; phoneZoomFocus '50% 50%'; scrub 0.6.
phone: The same drawing on the portrait crop, more of it down at the start, the camera pulling back at an even pace and the note under the sheet from the first frame; hold 1.5. Data-saving devices get the finished drawing.

name: Thumbnail becomes the stage
summary: A two-line statement sits over a row of small 16:9 thumbnails whose middle one is a keyhole onto a full-screen chapter; as the page scrolls the neighbours tuck behind it, the keyhole rises and opens to full bleed, and the statement's first line passes through its edge, ink outside and paper inside, to settle as the chapter's heading. It opens a product, a place or a film chapter from one strong muted loop or one strong picture.
place: In the middle, as the door from the intro into the showcase or the work; the opened picture carries the chapter's feature notes on a band at its foot.
content: One chapter picture or muted loop of 8-15 s (16:9, 1920x1080 or more, 8MB at most, with a poster; for software, a screen recording of the product), its subject inside the central 75% x 70% (that crop is the thumbnail) and its upper left calm and dark for the white heading; a 4:5 cut for phones. One or two satellite stills a side, 16:9, of neighbouring chapters in the same grade. No text burned into the pictures. A statement of up to two lines of 20 characters or fewer, whose first line names the chapter; an optional note under the heading; four feature items of a 2-3 word label and 16 words or fewer.
options: hold 2 (1.4-2.6); phoneHold 1.6 (1.4-2.6); phone 'same' | 'rest'; scrub 0.5, true with Lenis (0-0.8); thumb 0.17 (0.12-0.24) thumbnail width as a share of the row; radius, the page's --radius or 0 (0-16 px), always 0 at full bleed; shade 0.3 (0-0.6) flat scrim over the picture under the heading; band auto (0-0.85) the band behind the notes; heading 0.15 (0.1-0.25) where the heading settles; nav '', the selector of a fixed nav that gets is-on-dark over the picture.
phone: The same opening with the keyhole starting at half the width and its neighbours running off the edges; the first two feature notes show; hold 1.6.

name: Peel, tear and drag
summary: A physical thing brings in the next section: in the default drag a cloud deck closes over the old chapter and a huge photographed plane breaks out of it and pulls the next page in behind it through a seam that stays under its wings; peel lifts a sticker off the page, and tear rips the old ground along a ragged line and rolls it away. It is a change of section with a character, for a brand that moves things or does not take itself too seriously, once or twice a page.
place: Between two sections. Drag in the middle of the page, bringing in two or three quotes or a short list; peel on a hero or a footer; tear at a change of chapter. The new page has exactly the ground of the section that follows.
content: Drag: a top-down landscape photograph for the old chapter (sea, coast, fields from the air) with a closing line of 4-10 words; a cut-out photograph of a plane seen straight from above or below, nose to the right, about 2400px long, its wingspan about its length (without one the scene draws a plain jet, fit for a sketch only); up to seven soft-edged cut-outs of cloud for the deck; a new page with a heading of 3-8 words, two or three short real quotes or 3-12 rows, an optional aside of 20 words or fewer, and a wide photograph along its foot. The new page must fit one screen. Peel: the page's words and one photograph as the sticker (a second state of it optional). Tear: two chapters' words on two grounds, nothing else.
options: mode 'drag' | 'peel' | 'tear'. Drag: dir 'ltr' | 'rtl' (for a second use on one page); hold 3 (1.5-4; 2 without the cloud); phoneHold 2.2 (1.5-3.5); phone 'vertical' | 'rest'; scrub 0.6, true with Lenis; object 'jet' | 'none', what to paint with no cut-out; len 0.8 (0.3-0.9) length as a share of the width; phoneLen 0.62 (0.4-0.8); grow 1.25 (1-1.35), phoneGrow 1.15; apex and sweep (measured from the cut-out); bleed true; shadow true; veil true (false skips the cloud); tint 0.35 (0-0.7). Peel and tear: hold and phoneHold 1.5 (1-3); angle -34 peel, 163 tear (phoneAngle -58 / 163); band 0.09 (0.05-0.15); from and to (0.12-0.86 peel, 0.04-0.85 tear); lift true (peel); tilt 11.25, at 0.55 and phoneAt 0.5 (0.3-0.7), seed 11 (tear).
phone: Drag turns vertical: the plane flies bottom to top, nose up, and drags the page in from below; hold 2.2. Under 360px wide or 560px tall, the finished composition.

name: Raster cut between chapters
summary: On a held stage the next chapter's ground (a picture, a texture or a flat colour) prints over the current one through a raster of horizontal slats with whole-pixel edges, while the chapter title, drawn twice in exact register, changes from the old ink to the new one line by line without ever breaking. It is the one repeating joint of a site, between flat grounds or full-bleed pictures, always the same pattern and the same direction.
place: Between two sections, carrying the title of the one it opens (the intro, the work, the menu, the rooms, the contact). Up to three a page, three or more screens apart, never in neighbouring sections.
content: Two grounds: A, the current chapter (a full-bleed picture with a calm middle band, or flat), and B, the next (a full-bleed picture, a calm texture or a flat colour); pictures 16:10 or wider, 2400px or more. Four colours, --a-ground, --a-ink, --b-ground and --b-ink, each ink 7:1 or better on its ground and the two grounds 50 or more apart in lightness; the next section's background is exactly --b-ground. A title of 2-4 words, 22 characters at most, written in both layers, and a deck of 12-22 words in B only. Nothing else on the stage.
options: pattern 'slats' | 'blinds' | 'bands' | 'halftone' (flat B only); count 12 (slats 3-24, bands 3-8, blinds 2-5); phoneCount 12; order 'interlace' | 'bottom' | 'top' (a footer curtain) | 'centre' | 'shuffle' (blinds 'right' | 'left'); steps 4 (0-8) whole steps a slat grows in; amount 0.40 (0.2-0.5) stagger spread; ease 'power2.out' | 'none' | 'power3.out'; flip 0.5 (0.25-1); hold 1.2 (0.8-2; above 1.5 only with the bands line); phoneHold 1.2 (0.8-2); phone 'same' | 'rest'; fold 'auto' (a B picture lifts off the stage's foot so the next section joins on flat ground) | false; cell 10 (4-24) halftone pitch, phoneCell 8; seed 7; nav '', the selector of a fixed nav that takes each ground's ink; scrub 0.5, true with Lenis.
phone: The same cut with twelve slats and the title fitted to two lines; hold 1.2.

name: Letter physics
summary: A bold claim stands readable on a dark stage, breathes in, then bursts apart in true 3D, every letter flying off on its own path with spin and a little gravity, while a disc of light opens from its centre and a one-sentence answer flies out of depth and lands dark on the light as it opens, the light growing on until it floods the stage from top to bottom. It opens a chapter with a claim of 12-36 characters and needs no picture.
place: In the middle, as the opening of a chapter (the intro, the about, the work, the features): the claim is its heading and the answer its first sentence. Not for the first screen, where the answer would arrive only halfway through the scroll.
content: One claim of 12-36 characters (40 at most), fitted to two lines; one answering sentence of 40-90 characters (a longer one flies in by words); two optional side labels of 1-3 words in sentence case. Optional: one dark landscape photograph or render, 2400x1350 or more, mean luminance 20% or less, with its subject or a light source dead centre where the disc opens, and a 9:16 crop for phones. Four colours: a near-black ground, the light, the ink of the answer and the paper of the claim. On a 390px phone a claim over 30 characters sets below 40px: keep it short.
options: hold 1.8 (1.4-2.4); phoneHold 1.5 (1.2-2.2); phone 'same' | 'rest'; scrub 0.8, true with Lenis; exit 'burst' (3D) | 'detonate' (flat, wider, fast spin) | 'crumble' (the letters drop away in place, the middle first); spread 0.36 (0.3-0.45) burst radius; depth 520 (380-540) px the centre letters come nearest; gravity 0.22 (0.12-0.3); light 'white' | 'warm' | any CSS colour | 'none' (no disc: the answer lands in paper on the dark); disc 1.1 (0.5-1.2) diameter as a share of the height; phoneDisc 1.15 (0.9-1.3); payoff 'land' | 'pass' (only when the next section continues the sentence); intro false (true gathers the letters on load when the scene opens the page); particles 'auto' | 'chars' | 'words'; seed 0.
phone: The same burst with phone numbers: the claim at 13.5vw on up to two lines, the labels hidden, words as the particles for a long claim or a slow device; hold 1.5.

name: Object rides through giant type
summary: A short quote set in huge capitals fills a held stage while one cut-out object falls down through it: each line parts at its word gap around the object, closes behind it and turns from a muted tone to full ink as it passes, until the object swells, knocks the last lines into tumbling letters, drops out, and the whole quote stands closed in ink. It is for a statement worth reading slowly, paired with one clean cut-out: fashion, food and drink, jewellery, a personal brand.
place: In the middle, on the testimonial, the manifesto or the about: one short quote with its credit. Once per page.
content: One quote or manifesto of 3-5 lines (four reads best), 12-20 words in all, 10-14 characters a line (15 at most) with a word gap near the middle of each, written in sentence case (the CSS sets capitals). Few short lines are what make the type giant, about 10vw or more at 1440; six or seven lines set it near 90px, which reads as a paragraph rather than a wall. A longer sentence stays a static statement elsewhere, and the scene carries one phrase of it. On a phone, 12 words or fewer, or phone 'rest'. The client's own words or its own people's, with a credit of 5 words or fewer; never an invented customer. No eyebrow. One object as a transparent WebP or PNG cropped close, a compact silhouette (aspect 0.7-1.4: a coin, a watch head, a stone, a cap, a cup), clean alpha, no baked shadow, about 900px or more, standing apart from both ground and ink by itself: the product when there is one, otherwise a thing of its world that no visitor could take for the product. Set size 1.7 or more, so the object stands about a third of the stage high and reads as the subject, not a bead between words; tumble keeps its face to the camera, flip shows it edge-on between lines. Without a cut-out, a photograph of a round thing (a clock face, a coin, a record) made square and round in CSS. Flip mode takes a flat thing with two faces.
options: hold 3 (2.5-4); phoneHold 3.5 (2.5-4.5); phone 'same' | 'rest' (a poster frame); reflow true (the lines are re-wrapped for the phone); travel 'auto' | true | false; scrub 0.6, true with Lenis; mode 'tumble' | 'flip' (spins like a coin); rim '', the edge colour in flip; edge 'round' | 'flat'; thick 0.06 (0.02-0.14); size 1.45 (1.1-1.8) the object's box in type sizes, phoneSize 1.9 (1.3-2.2); push 1.4 (1.1-1.8), phonePush; radius 2.4 (1.8-3) reach of the wake; falloff 2.5 (1.5 soft and wide, 4 a tight slit); lag 0.15 (0-0.35) seconds the halves trail; follow 0.4 (0-1); enter 'above' | 'inside'; tilt [-9, 15] degrees at the first and the last line; exit 'break' (the last lines burst into letters that fly home) | 'fall' (it only swells and drops out); shatter 3 (1-6) lines that break; giants 2 (0-3); seed 7; grow 2.4 (1.2-2.8); tip 45 (0-70); drift 0.07 (0-0.12), phoneDrift 0.09; rest 0.5 (0.42-0.7) opacity of the lines not yet reached; fill 0.86 (0.7-0.92), phoneFill 0.88.
phone: The same fall, the halves re-wrapped into as many phone lines as fill the screen at the largest size; hold 3.5.

name: Scroll-turned drum
summary: A list of short names sits on the face of a horizontal drum that the scroll cranks like a slot reel, the name on the front line in full ink while the others roll back into ghosted depth; give every name a photograph and a second drum of pictures turns against it on the right, each picture holding while its name is up. It turns a list of places, products, dishes, rooms or real clients into one pinned set piece.
place: In the middle, on the list, the work or the proof: where eight to twenty names would otherwise sit in a column or a row of logos.
content: Eight to twenty names (3-30 work), 1-3 words and 22 characters at most each, with optional detail of five words or fewer (a city, a year, a sector) and an optional landscape photograph (900, 1200 and 1600px wide). Real names only: clients only when they are real clients; otherwise the subject's own places, products, dishes or rooms. A statement of two lines, and an optional closing line of seven words or fewer with a button. One ground and one ink; the ghosts are the ink at a lower opacity, never a second hue.
options: hold 0.16 a name + 0.2, kept to 1.6-3.2 (1-4); tempo 0.16 (0.12-0.22) screens a name, when hold is not given; scrub true with Stage.smooth(), else 0.5; size 1 (0.7-1.4) the name size; spacing 1.03 (0.9-1.3); radius 0.5, phone 0.34 (0.3-0.6) the drum's radius as a share of the height; depth 3 (2.5-8); width 56, phone 82 (40-72) the widest name in vw; ghost 0.32 (0.18-0.45); ghostFar 0.1 (0.04-0.12); highlight 'ink' | 'accent'; count true, "4 of 15"; of 'of'; pictures true; gear 'counter' | 'same'; pictureTurn 'step' | 'smooth'; pictureStep 36 (24-50) degrees between pictures; ends true (the first and the last picture fill the right of the screen); detent false (true settles on a name when the scroll stops; use it for the picture drum under Lenis); phone 'same' | 'rest'.
phone: The drum stays, since a portrait screen suits a reel, with phone numbers and the picture drum turning behind a full-width window above the names. Under 340px wide, or when the longest name cannot fit at 26px, the finished list.

name: Type re-layout
summary: A short list in giant capitals on a held, picture-free stage is re-set three times by the scroll: its ragged lines spread into a justified slab and the short last item slides flush right, then the small heading relays letter by letter to the opposite corner, the slab folds line by line into a small index and the heading swells over a paragraph. It is for what a studio makes, a programme or a set of benefits, on editorial and type-led pages.
place: In the middle, on the services, the programme or the about: a section that is really a list of four to six things.
content: No pictures. A heading of one word, 4-7 letters (the section's name); a list of 3-6 items (up to twelve work, smaller), one line each: every item but the last 2-4 words and 11-16 characters, the last 1-2 words and 9 characters at most, no item but the last a single word; a paragraph of about 25 words, three lines at most at statement size. One display face in capitals, one flat ground and one ink at 7:1.
options: hold 3 (2-4); phone 'rest' (the finished composition) | 'same' (a poster version that only spreads and slides); phoneHold 1.5 (1-3); scrub 0.8, true with Lenis; size 12 (6-16) the largest display size in vw; gap 1.2 (0.6-3) the tightest justified gap in em; fill 0.94 (0.8-0.98); cols 12 (4-12) columns the list may span; index 'auto' or 14-32 px; relay true (false keeps the heading still and lands the index under it); grow true (the heading swells after the relay); dot 0.3 (0.12-0.4) a letter's scale in flight; stagger 0.016 (0.010-0.025).
phone: By default the finished composition (heading, justified slab, paragraph) as an ordinary section; with phone 'same', a poster that spreads and slides the list without the relay or the fold.

name: Wordmark under strain
summary: The brand's name in giant type is held and put under load by the scroll: it is crushed onto its baseline and springs back, recedes into a stepped echo of stacked copies, and its one straight letter loosens, falls out and lands flat as the call-to-action button. It is the closing moment of a page for a brand with a short, strong name.
place: At the end of the page, as the call to action and the footer in one; anything after it keeps the same ground. Once per page. For a loud name (a band, a launch, a sports brand, a studio that shouts): on a calm house, a guesthouse, a craft or a care practice the strain and the dropped letter read as a broken name, so redraw the scenes. At rest the name reads whole.
content: One word of 4-8 letters (4-6 best), the brand's name or a closing word, in capitals, with one straight letter (I, l or 1) that is neither the first nor the last (without one, a square full stop is added and falls instead). A button label of 2-3 words, 18 characters at most; a sentence of 45 characters or more about the offer and a place line for the top row; a meta row of three short items (an email, a city, a link). Type only: one heavy display face, one flat ground shared with what follows, one ink at 7:1, an optional accent for the landed button.
options: hold 2.5 (1.5-4); phoneHold 2 (1.5-3); phone 'same' | 'rest'; scrub 0.8, true with Lenis; copies 6 (4-8) in the echo; step 1/13 (1/16-1/9) scale each copy loses; shift 2 (1-4) % of the word's height each copy sinks; squash 0.10 (0-0.15); spring 3 (1.5-3); drop true (false keeps the word whole and the button under it from the start); letter auto, the letter that falls; size [300, 64] the landed button in px, phoneSize [240, 52]; radius 0 (0-8); accent '', the button's colour as it lands; reveal 'wipe' | 'fade'; fill 0.92 (0.8-0.96); maxHeight 0.42 (0.3-0.45); stretch 'normal'; phoneStretch 'condensed'.
phone: The same strain with phone numbers: the word fitted to the width (narrower if the face has a width axis), the meta row in two lines; hold 2.
